To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) imported inputs are important in explaining agricultural productivity; (2) imported inputs are more important in LICs than in other countries; and (3) the negative impacts of climate change are more severe in LICs than other countries, and imported intermediate inputs can mitigate such effects.

(1) agricultural TFP is lower in LICs than in other countries, (2) agricultural TFP has been growing in LICs, but the growth rate is lower than in other countries; (3) imported inputs are important in explaining cross-country differences in agricultural TFP, and (4) climate is also an important determinant of agricultural TFP, but the effect varies across countries.

(1) agricultural TFP growth rates in the 1990-2015 period have been higher in high-income countries than LICs and the former have also been able to reduce agricultural TFP gaps relative to the latter; (2) imported inputs are an important source of TFP gains in agriculture, particularly in LICs, where their contribution to agricultural TFP growth was higher than in high-income countries; and (3) climate shocks have a negative effect on agricultural TFP growth in LIC
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of imported intermediate inputs and weather in agricultural TFP growth, and their interactions.
how the import of intermediate inputs can be used as a tool to mitigate the impact of climate change in the agricultural sector, particularly in LICs.
two important issues: 1) how agricultural productivity can be improved, and 2) how the adverse effects of climate change on agricultural productivity can be reduced.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for LICs, the negative impacts of climate change can be mitigated by increasing the use of imported inputs.
, for LICs, the benefits of imported inputs are larger than the costs of climate change, while for high-income countries (HICs) the opposite is true.
, while climate change is a major threat to agricultural TFP, the negative impact of climate change can be mitigated by the use of more modern inputs, especially for LICs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the agricultural TFP growth is a result of the interplay between imported intermediate inputs and the climate.
imported inputs are a key driver of agricultural TFP and can mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change.
the import of intermediate inputs is an important driver of agricultural productivity growth and that this is especially true for LICs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in LICs, the import component of intermediate input can be a useful tool to offset negative effects of climate on agricultural productivity.
LICs that import more intermediate inputs tend to be less affected by climate shocks.
, while climate is a key factor affecting agricultural TFP, the negative effects can be reduced by importing more intermediate inputs.
